public_health_question.v: What were the epidemiologic, clinical and genomic characteristics of a statewide serogroup Y meningococcal disease outbreak in Virginia lacking a defined at-risk population, and how was it controlled?

ev.q: In a Virginia outbreak, 36 cases of serogroup Y meningococcal disease occurred during August 2022–March 2024; seven (19.4%) patients died.
Patients lacked common exposures or affiliations. Vaccination was recommended for close contacts within the patient age range.
Statewide Outbreak of Neisseria meningitidis Serogroup Y, Sequence Type 1466 — Virginia, 2022–2024
In August 2022, the Virginia Department of Health (VDH) began investigating an IMD outbreak in Virginia’s Eastern Health Planning Region.
VDH conducted active case finding by monitoring syndromic surveillance † and reviewing medical records of patients with suspected meningitis or meningococcemia.
VDH conducted standard public health interviews with patients to identify close contacts.
Syndromic surveillance was conducted through the Virginia Electronic Surveillance System for the Early Notification of Community-based Epidemics.
The average social vulnerability index score § of patients’ residential U.S. Census Bureau tracts was 0.63

equity.level_reason: The Discussion frames a disparity (disproportionately affected Black persons: 83% of Southwest cases vs 12% of residents) and reports patients' mean tract SVI 0.63 (fatal 0.73) vs 0.4 statewide, interpreting it as access challenges. Contrasts are set against population referents, as in the shares-vs-births precedent.

level_alternative.reason: Social vulnerability and challenges in accessing medical care are named as explanations of poor outcomes; but they explain fatality, not clearly the racial disparity, and contrasts are side by side (a strict reading gives 2).

equity.equity_measurement: Racial shares of cases are compared with the resident population only for the Southwest Region; Table race has only Black and White non-Hispanic. SES is the mean tract SVI of patients' residences vs the statewide average, with no test.

notes: No analytic procedures: the 'sensitivity' cue is antimicrobial susceptibility, and WGS only confirms case status. Comparisons (CFR vs national range, SVI vs state, % Black vs region) are side by side with no computed contrast. Data focus could be read as limited (a 36-case series), but quantities and referent comparisons are reported.
